values: Entity-relationship diagram: student, enrolment, section, component, score
Grading structure hangs off section, not student; reviewed by all three members
Migration: core tables, keys and constraints
Migration runs clean on an empty database and is reversible
Consent state in schema plus a guard on every write path
No row is written for a student who has not granted storage consent
Repository layer using parameterised queries only
No string-concatenated SQL anywhere in the repository
Section grading structure storage (components, weights, mode, deadline)
One section row carries the full structure; no per-student duplication
Server-side weight-sum validation with explanatory rejection
A structure summing to 95 percent is rejected with a message naming the gap
Join-by-code: code generation, uniqueness, join operation
Second account joins an existing section and sees the same structure
Two accounts share one section through the API alone
A score cannot reference a component from another section
Attendance feeds the weighted score when the course weights it
Scores post and read back correctly for the authenticated student only
Calculation endpoints: current score, required score, projection
Every numeric field in the response comes from the engine, none computed in the route
Values are per student and editable
Flag plus previous grade stored and readable by the GPAX path
Cascade deletion of all data belonging to one student
Deleting the student row leaves no orphan score, enrolment or consent row
docker compose up gives a running API and an empty database on a teammate's machine
Deploy to Render or Railway with public HTTPS
Public URL returns 200 on /health with a valid certificate
No credential appears in the repository; app boots from env vars only
LINE channel and LIFF application registration
Channel secret and access token available as environment variables
Webhook endpoint with HMAC-SHA256 signature verification over the raw body
A request with a modified body is rejected before parsing
Return HTTP 200 immediately, process the event asynchronously
Webhook responds under one second regardless of downstream work
Migration runner wired into the deploy pipeline
A push to main applies pending migrations before the new image serves traffic
Branch protection and mandatory PR review
Direct pushes to main are rejected; one approval required
GitHub Actions running lint and Jest on every pull request
A PR with a failing engine test cannot be merged
Define engine public API: function signatures, input and output shapes
Signatures documented and agreed; no function takes a database handle or a clock
REST contract: endpoints, methods, parameters, JSON responses
Written and agreed before implementation so client and server can proceed in parallel
Figma wireframes for the seven core screens
Consent, setup, join, score entry, OCR confirmation, course detail, GPAX comparison all drawn
Grade scale, letter thresholds and grade-point constants
Constants live in one module; no magic number appears elsewhere
Returns score and the weight actually graded so far; pure, no I/O
Minimum required score on remaining assessments
Matches the RogerHub formula on three hand-checked cases
Returns unreachable when required score exceeds the maximum obtainable
Projects a letter only when the course is criterion-referenced
Norm-referenced branch: score only, no letter grade
Returns a null letter with an explicit reason code, never a guess
GPAX projection from current GPA and credits earned
Reproduces a hand-calculated GPAX for a three-course scenario
Express skeleton: routing, request validation, error handling
Invalid payloads return a structured 400 rather than a stack trace
Stay versus withdraw comparison across grade scenarios
Returns both branches plus the delta; never returns a recommendation
Engine unit tests covering the boundary cases
Zero-weight component, unreachable target, norm-referenced, weights not summing, repeated course all covered
Returns the projected GPAX and the name of the rule applied
Response carries both branches and the disclaimer text field
Consent endpoints: grant, withdraw, delete account
Storage consent and cross-border consent are separate flags with separate endpoints
An expired or forged token is refused before any handler runs
A student records a score end to end without leaving the chat
React and Vite setup, LIFF SDK init, auth bootstrap
App opens inside LINE and identifies the student server-side
Manual grading-structure entry as a complete alternative path
A student can set up any course without ever using the camera
Menu appears in the chat and routes to the correct flow or LIFF screen
Course list and course detail screens
Shows current weighted score and required score per course
Grading structure setup and edit screen
Weights must sum to 100 before save is enabled; server still revalidates
Wrong code produces a clear Thai error, not a blank screen
Entry from LIFF and entry from quick reply produce identical stored data
Disclaimer component bound to every comparison render
It is structurally impossible to render a comparison without the estimate-not-advice text
Two separate consent screens: storage, then cross-border transfer
Declining the second still gives a fully working app; the two are never bundled into one tick box
Cross-border consent flag routing explanation to template when declined
With the flag off, no request reaches the external service at all
A push reaches a test account
Deadline scheduler: unreachable target before withdrawal deadline triggers a push
Job runs on a schedule, is idempotent, and never notifies the same student twice for one course
GPAX and withdrawal comparison view with Recharts
Stay and withdraw branches shown side by side with the numeric delta
Deletion is user-initiated, confirmed, and irreversible
Thai copy and terminology pass across all screens
One reviewer who did not write the screens reads every string for clarity
Produces a complete, correct Thai explanation with the language model switched off
Anonymised payload builder for the external service
Payload contains no name, LINE user id, course id or individual component score
Integration test: tampered webhook body is rejected
Test fails if signature verification is removed
Integration test: expired ID token is refused
Test fails if verification is downgraded to decode-only
Lists lost credits, prerequisite dependencies, re-offering and fee implications
System test of the full flow on the deployed instance
Set up, join from a second account, record, calculate, receive notification, all on production
PDPA data inventory: what is stored, why, where it goes, how it is deleted
One page listing every stored field and its lawful basis, ready for the report
UAT protocol: task list, observation sheet, consent for testers
Written before testing so results are comparable across participants
Matches what was built, not what was proposed in August
A teammate clones and runs the stack from the README alone
Tesseract in the container with Thai and English language data
Image never leaves the container; OCR runs with no outbound request
Syllabus table parsing into components and weights
Extracts a usable draft from five real KKU syllabus photos
Nothing extracted is stored until the student confirms or corrects it
Gemini client with timeout and fallback to template
A timeout or error silently falls back to the template, never to an empty reply
Numeric verification of model output against the engine
A deliberately altered number causes the response to be discarded and the template used
Integration test: incorrect model number is discarded
Injected wrong number never reaches the student
UAT sessions with 5 to 8 DME students and result recording
Per participant: which tasks completed unaided, and the step at which any failure occurred
Includes UAT results and an honest limitations section
Shows the full loop including the withdrawal comparison
Rehearsed to time by all three members

values: Sunny Beach Day, extended to eight steps. Cool teal at the start of the project, hot coral at submission.
Recommended platform implementation order first, followed by remaining tasks in their original order. Target weeks and priorities remain unchanged.
Owner, Status and Notes. Their headers are the coral ones.
The Summary sheet. Every cell there is a formula counting the Tasks sheet.
Insert a row, give it an ID with the category prefix and the next free number, then re-sort. Dropdowns and Summary formulas already cover rows 2 to 400.
Row order is the recommended work sequence, not a deadline sort. Check Depends on before starting; other team members may own prerequisites. Status is maintained separately in the online tracker.
Column A is the solid chip; the rest of the row is the same hue at 22 per cent, which keeps text contrast above 6.9 to 1
The week this should be finished. Change it and the row colour when a task slips, or the colours stop telling the truth.
Week number 1 to 8, used for sorting. 1 is September W1.
Category prefix plus a number. Stable: never renumber, because Depends on points at these. Re-sorting never changes an ID, which is the point of having them.
Type of work. The ten categories agreed for this project.
One deliverable, small enough for one person to finish inside a week.
Which numbered item in section 4.1 (In scope) or section 8 (Methodology) of the proposal this satisfies. Every scope item should appear at least once.
One name. Two owners means nobody owns it. Dropdown reads the People sheet.
To do, Doing, Blocked, Done. Blocked is not a synonym for To do: it means another task must finish first, and Notes should say which.
P0, P1, P2. Defined below. Inside a week, clear the P0 block before P1.
IDs that must reach Done before this can start. This column, not the week, is what actually determines order. A task whose dependency sits in a later week is a planning error: fix it when you see it.
Person-days of real work, not calendar days. An estimate you know is optimistic is worse than no estimate.
Yes means the task touches stored personal data or sends data abroad, shown in bold teal. A Yes task is not Done until the three PDPA rules below hold.
The observable condition that ends the task. Written before starting.
On the critical path. Something else cannot start until this is done, or the demo cannot be shown without it. Slipping a P0 slips the project.
Required by the proposal scope but blocking nobody. Slipping it costs completeness, not the schedule.
Cuttable. Section 8.6.2 names the cut order: the language model first, because the Thai template is already a complete answer, then OCR, because manual entry is a full alternative.
Apply to every task whose Privacy check is Yes
If the code path writes student data, it checks the storage consent flag first and stores nothing without it (In scope 23).
If the code path sends data outside Thailand, it checks the separate cross-border flag and falls back to the Thai template (In scope 24, 25).
If a payload leaves the system, it carries only anonymised numeric values: no name, LINE user id, course id, or individual component score (In scope 26).
How a filled row should look
